title: Panique à la photocopieuse  (Panic at the Photocopier)

segments.t: In the quiet hallway at ASK, Gabriel Sarda confides his panic to Andrea Martel. His star client Sandrine Kiberlain is jeopardizing a major movie role to pursue a risky career in comedy. Andrea tries to soothe Gabriel while reflecting on her own stressful routine as a working mother, with sudden consequences. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Tout va très mal avec Sandrine Kiberlain.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe sur son tournage?
Elle veut abandonner le film de Thompson.
Ne panique pas, tu vas arranger ça.
Elle veut faire du stand-up maintenant!
Respire Gabriel, tout va bien se passer.
Et toi, comment se passe ta vie?
Je gère ma vie toute seule.
Ce n'est pas trop dur avec Flora?
C'est comme faire une randonnée en tongs!
Mais le bébé va bien ici?
Oui, elle est très calme aujourd'hui.
Attends, où est passée ma fille?
Merde, je l'ai oubliée à la photocopieuse!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Tout va très mal avec Sandrine Kiberlain.
'Everything goes very badly with Sandrine Kiberlain.' Gabriel shares his mounting stress regarding his unpredictable star client. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'goes'.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe sur son tournage?
'What is happening on her shoot?' Andrea inquires about the production problems. The standard spoken question formula at the front turns the statement about 'happens' into a natural inquiry.
Elle veut abandonner le film de Thompson.

'She wants to abandon Thompson's film.' Gabriel reveals that Sandrine plans to walk away from the prestigious project. The verb meaning 'wants' pairs naturally with the noun for 'film' in everyday conversation.
Ne panique pas, tu vas arranger ça.
'Do not panic, you will fix that.' Andrea encourages her distressed partner to stay grounded. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'panic'.
Elle veut faire du stand-up maintenant!

'She wants to do stand-up now!' Gabriel explains that the dramatic actress has suddenly fallen in love with comedy. The verb meaning 'wants' pairs naturally with the noun for 'stand-up comedy' in everyday conversation.
Respire Gabriel, tout va bien se passer.
'Breathe Gabriel, everything will go well.' The reflexive pronoun sits right in front of the verb for 'breathe', turning the action back onto the subject.
Et toi, comment se passe ta vie?

'And you, how is your life going?' Gabriel changes the subject to ask about Andrea's domestic situation. The reflexive pronoun sits right in front of the verb for 'is going', turning the action back onto the subject.
Je gère ma vie toute seule.
'I manage my life all alone.' Andrea explains her exhausting daily schedule since Colette's departure. The adjective meaning 'alone' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Ce n'est pas trop dur avec Flora?
'Is it not too hard with Flora?' Gabriel gently asks about Andrea's infant daughter. The descriptive adjective for 'hard' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
C'est comme faire une randonnée en tongs!
'It is like hiking in flip-flops!' Andrea humorously summarizes the struggle of balancing baby care and agency work. Notice how 'do' leads directly into the noun meaning 'hike'.
Mais le bébé va bien ici?

'But the baby is doing well here?' Gabriel observes that the child seems surprisingly quiet at the office. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'does' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
Oui, elle est très calme aujourd'hui.

'Yes, she is very calm today.' Andrea proudly notes that her baby has been well-behaved. In spoken French, the little word before 'the next word' drops its final vowel and attaches with an apostrophe.
Attends, où est passée ma fille?
'Wait, where did my daughter go?' Andrea suddenly stops in her tracks with rising unease. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past participle for 'gone'.
Merde, je l'ai oubliée à la photocopieuse!

'Damn, I forgot her at the photocopier!' Andrea rushes frantically down the corridor to retrieve her child. Notice how 'have' leads directly into the noun meaning 'photocopier'. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
Tout va très mal avec Sandrine Kiberlain.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe sur son tournage?
Elle veut abandonner le film de Thompson.
Ne panique pas, tu vas arranger ça.
Elle veut faire du stand-up maintenant!
Respire Gabriel, tout va bien se passer.
Et toi, comment se passe ta vie?
Je gère ma vie toute seule.

C'est comme faire une randonnée en tongs!
Mais le bébé va bien ici?
Oui, elle est très calme aujourd'hui.
Attends, où est passée ma fille?
Merde, je l'ai oubliée à la photocopieuse!

Startled by her own distraction, Andrea sprints across the office to rescue baby Flora from the copy room. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'goes' and 'happens'. You'll catch them now. See you next time.
Flora dort tranquillement à côté du papier!
